overall_assessment:
Private TQA result: acceptable for the complete current nine-path package, with no new material source or test-quality defect found. This is advisory only: it neither approves ST-CON-01 delivery nor waives external proof. I inspected all named current paths: ChannelsService, receipt convergence, Evolution webhook, Meta client and unit spec, onboarding PG E2E, test helper, compiled browser runner, and Web Playwright suite; named original diffs API f134bd1 and Web d33c82c and the current spec-only dirty delta were reviewed. Current manifest 39c7b8d31e963ae4e5a5667d960ef84d5277a070e044a95b45890802e24d29a7 is consistent with one changed Meta unit spec and eight unchanged paths.

Five questions: Q1 contract alignment is yes: the new test exercises the D02 requirement that the current grant belong to the configured app before resource lookup, alongside existing scoped-token, scope/WABA-intersection, bounded-page, typed-error, and fixed-host behavior. Q2 pass-the-test/brittleness is acceptable: the fixture is structurally valid except for app_id and includes a viable matching second phone-page response, so removing app equality resolves instead of rejecting and fails the oracle; it is not dependent on an undefined mock fallback. Q3 assertion efficacy is strong: it checks the real adapter rejection class and catalog code, exactly one authenticated debug_token request with the candidate token, and zero phone lookup. Q4 assertion efficiency is acceptable: one direct unit operation, deterministic controlled fetches, no sleep, retry, focus, skip, or test-only product path; the extra fallback response exists solely to establish the mutant relation. Q5 coverage is sufficient for the required private source claim: adapter positives/negatives cover grant shape, revoked and wrong-app grants, scopes and WABA intersection, page/cursor/budget/malformed failures; PG/BFF coverage uses real Nest/session/CSRF/Prisma/PostgreSQL and preserves failure-state invariants; browser coverage remains honest historical evidence on unchanged consumer bytes. It is not sufficient for real official-provider proof.

Applicable 14-step audit: framed the bounded current claim; accepted test-after because the production guard already existed and a manufactured source RED would not be evidence; scanned for bypasses; matched each assertion to the claimed guard; checked mock/fallback behavior; checked META_CLIENT token/class parity; checked safe typed versus generic failure behavior; assessed assertion strength and execution cost; checked the recorded command and CI-equivalent evidence; checked build/runtime separation; checked platform/layer limits; issued residual-risk cards; retained uncertainty; and checked D01-D10 plus module adherence. The direct unit uses MetaHttpClient, while the BFF E2E overrides the exact META_CLIENT port but delegates selected cases to the real adapter behind controlled fetch; helpers and browser runner preserve the same method, bounded paging, typed error, and production token shape. This is legitimate external-I/O doubling, not a claim of real Meta.

Architecture and code quality are acceptable: shared exact-attempt convergence is idempotent; official verification revalidates a scoped grant before at-most-two pages; Graph host and redirect policy are fixed; ChannelsService maps only MetaIndisponivelError to the safe 503 and preserves generic/auth/CAS failures; Evolution convergence retains identity, generation, epoch, receipt, and attempt fences. Tests are layered rather than duplicated bypasses. Performance is acceptable for this change: it adds a constant-cost unit case and leaves production/build bytes unchanged; existing code retains two-page, 10-second-request, and 45-second-lease bounds. Capacity, SLOs, continuous health, and real-provider latency remain unproven. Security is acceptable within the private test scope: wrong-app rejection strengthens audience isolation, no global-token fallback or raw provider disclosure was found in the reviewed paths, and malformed provider data is fail-closed; the existing dependency-security exposure remains a separate release constraint.

Command/CI/build/platform/layer/freshness matrix: evidence records one canonical API command, bash scripts/test-channels-local.sh api, exit 0 with 174 unit and 288 PostgreSQL tests plus 22 migrations; I did not rerun it. Web28 and browser47 are immutable h evidence only, on unchanged source, not a j all-537 or j browser run. tsconfig.build excludes test and spec files, so the spec-only j change is build-neutral. The served production image remains i, explicitly bridged from unchanged build inputs; it is not a j image build or freshness claim. The cp52 supplement resolves the private nonofficial post-restart human IN/OUT association with one new conversation, while preserving old history; it proves observed private recovery and association only, not official Meta, capacity, continuous health, or overall VAL-05.

Decision/module matrix: current source and tests preserve D01 canonical BU ownership; D02 app/grant/scope/WABA revalidation; D03 attempt/CAS/lease separation; D04 scoped encrypted credentials without global fallback; D05 distinct official phases and callback boundaries; D06 own Evolution identity/epoch/POST pairing; D07 separate observations and durable ownership; D08 scoped BFF/public/Typebot and shared message acceptance; D09 isolated local-first operation; and D10 serial principal-checkout discipline. integrations-and-channels, identity-and-tenancy, inbox-and-conversations, and audit-and-history remain aligned. D05-D07 remain operational Exceptions because their external gates are not satisfied. Review activity was read-only: no tests, builds, network, provider/runtime, source, Git, canon, goal, delegation, or worktree mutation was performed.
recommended_path: Allow root adjudication to consume this private TQA result, then require the separately mandated final reviewer. Keep ST-CON-01 Pending; do not claim official onboarding or overall delivery until the carry-forward external-proof and dependency-security gates are resolved.

findings.title: Official-channel VAL-05 proof remains unfulfilled
findings.rationale: Why now: the current API evidence, historical unchanged-browser evidence, build-neutral served-i bridge, and observed private nonofficial recovery/INOUT do not demonstrate real official OAuth, operator-selected test resource, subscription, official IN/OUT, and permitted official recovery. The package and supplement expressly retain this as Pending; it is a delivery gate, not a newly found source defect.
findings.suggested_action: Options: A, retain Pending with no delivery claim; B, conduct the governed real official VAL-05 sequence on the explicitly selected test resource after the required final review, preserving proof boundaries and recording results; C, treat nonofficial or historical evidence as official proof. Recommend B; C is not permitted.

findings.title: Known dependency-security exposure remains a pre-untrusted-user gate
findings.rationale: Why now: the bounded package records an existing dependency set with one critical and multiple high findings, constrained to a private OWNER/synthetic cohort. This audit found no new dependency mutation or masking test in the nine paths, but the unresolved risk remains relevant to the Security axis and cannot be converted into a general deployment claim.
findings.suggested_action: Options: A, retain the documented private controlled-cohort restriction; B, remediate and independently validate the dependency backlog in a separately governed package before admitting untrusted authenticated users; C, waive the exposure for broader use. Recommend B; C is not acceptable.
